$comment: Target profile for fireweed. The one target here for which the clearcut problem runs the other way: fireweed is THE colonist of burns, cutblocks, avalanche tracks and road cuts, so the open, high-NDVI signature of a regenerating block is exactly right and is not penalised.
habitat_note: Disturbed open ground at every elevation: burns, cutblocks 2-15 years after harvest, avalanche paths, road cuts and landings, and subalpine meadows. Shade-intolerant, so it fades as a block's canopy closes. Formerly Epilobium angustifolium / Chamerion angustifolium.

terrain_subweights.$comment: Terrain says little about a plant that tracks disturbance, not landform; slope carries most of what there is (very steep ground is rock, not fireweed).

observations.$comment: 131 AOI records, 625 Kootenays: the best-recorded target in the set. Dwarf fireweed (C. latifolium) grows on river gravel bars and alpine scree, a different habitat, so it is down-weighted.

aspect.$comment: Faint south preference only; 62% of records are on south-to-west slopes, about what open ground in this AOI offers anyway.

ndvi.$comment: Dense fireweed stands are lush; a sparse fresh burn is not yet a stand. Floor above yarrow's.

logging.$comment: No penalty. A credit for young blocks would be the honest model, but the logging term only multiplies logged cells and cannot lift them above unlogged open ground; the openness credit already ranks young, open blocks highly, and closes them out as their canopy shuts.

validation.$comment: Same contrast as yarrow: a closed-forest understory forb with shared collectors.
